We need to find min total cost to transform source string to target string by applying any number of transformations of characters individually. Each operation transforms one character x to y with a cost from given edges (original[i] -> changed[i] cost cost[i]). There may be multiple edges between same pair; we can pick minimal cost for each direct transformation. Also can transform via intermediate characters (like a -> c -> b) with sum cost; we need to compute cheapest cost to transform each character to each other character via any sequence, like all-pairs shortest path on 26 nodes (lowercase letters). Since cost lengths up to 2000, compute Floyd-Warshall (26^3 ~ 17576) trivial.

We need for each position i where source[i] != target[i], compute minimal cost to convert source[i] to target[i] via allowed transformations (including zero if same). If impossible for any position, answer -1. Else sum costs across positions.

Edge cases: may need to consider using multiple steps (transformation chain). Compute dist[26][26] initialized to INF; dist[c][c] = 0. For each edge (original[j], changed[j]), set dist[orig][ch] = min(dist[orig][ch], cost[j]) (taking min across parallel edges). Then Floyd.

Complexities: O(26^3 + n). n up to 1e5.

Return sum as int (may overflow 32-bit but Python fine). If any dist[src][tgt] INF, return -1.
